desc:
A pivot index of the integer array nums is an index whose left side and right side have the same sum. The left side is every element strictly before the index and the right side is every element strictly after it. An empty side counts as sum 0.

Return the leftmost pivot index, or -1 if none exists.

For example, in [1, 7, 3, 6, 5, 6] index 3 is the pivot: 1 + 7 + 3 = 11 = 5 + 6. In [2, 1, -1] index 0 is the pivot, because its left side is empty (sum 0) and 1 + (-1) = 0.
hints: For a fixed index i you could add up both sides directly. That costs O(n) per index, so what repeated work can you avoid?
Let total be the sum of the whole array. If you know the sum left of everything before i, the sum after i is total - left - nums[i].
Scan from left to right keeping a running left sum. At each index compare left with total - left - nums[i], and return the first index where they match.
editorial: Compute the total sum once. Then walk through the array while maintaining left, the sum of the elements before the current index. The right sum at index i is total - left - nums[i], so the index is a pivot exactly when left == total - left - nums[i]. Because we scan from the left and stop at the first match, we automatically return the leftmost pivot.

This is the prefix-sum idea in its lightest form: one pass for the total, one pass for the check, and only a couple of variables. Negative numbers and zeros need no special treatment, which is why the answer can be several indices apart even in short arrays (for instance every index of an all-zero array is a pivot, and the leftmost one is 0).
